---
title: "Kriging Interpolator"
date: 2026-09-17
categories: [tool, geostatistics]
description: "Upload sparse point samples (soil moisture, pH, pollution readings, anything measured at scattered locations) and predict a full continuous surface across the whole area — fitting a variogram model first, not just averaging nearby points. Runs entirely in your browser, powered by R."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a point file with a numeric column — soil moisture, pH,
pollutant concentration, anything measured at scattered sample
locations — pick that column, and this tool fits a variogram model to
how similar nearby points really are, then predicts a value everywhere
across the area, not just at the points you measured.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your browser
(R via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server, including
ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code never gets the
chance to see your data.
:::

```{.webgeods-r #kriging-interpolator-inspect-r .tool-cell}
#| package: sf, geojsonsf, jsonlite
library(sf)
library(geojsonsf)

pts <- NULL
for (path in c("/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip")) {
  pts <- tryCatch(st_read(path, quiet = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(pts)) break
}

EMPTY_FC <- list(type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"), features = list())

# A column counts as usable for kriging if it's already numeric, or if
# every non-missing value in it parses as a number (a common shape for
# a column read from a CSV-derived GeoJSON, where numbers can arrive as
# character strings) -- text/categorical columns are excluded rather
# than crashing later inside variogram() with an opaque type error.
looks_numeric <- function(v) {
  if (is.numeric(v)) return(TRUE)
  if (!is.character(v)) return(FALSE)
  non_na <- v[!is.na(v)]
  if (length(non_na) == 0) return(FALSE)
  suppressWarnings(!any(is.na(as.numeric(non_na))))
}

crs_warning <- NULL
summary_out <- NULL
features_out <- EMPTY_FC

if (!is.null(pts)) {
  original_crs <- st_crs(pts)
  if (is.na(original_crs)) {
    pts <- st_set_crs(pts, 4326)
    crs_warning <- "No CRS found in the uploaded file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."
    original_crs_label <- "Unknown (assumed WGS84)"
  } else {
    original_crs_label <- if (!is.na(original_crs$epsg)) paste0("EPSG:", original_crs$epsg) else original_crs$input
    if (is.na(original_crs$epsg) || original_crs$epsg != 4326) {
      pts <- st_transform(pts, 4326)
    }
  }

  geom_col <- attr(pts, "sf_column")
  cols <- setdiff(names(pts), geom_col)
  numeric_cols <- cols[sapply(cols, function(c) looks_numeric(pts[[c]]))]

  # Preview coloring: pick a default numeric column the same way
  # Compute's own "Value column" input defaults (prefer
  # "soil_moisture_pct", else the first numeric column found), so the
  # map shows a meaningful preview immediately after Upload/Load
  # example -- before the user has touched that selector at all, same
  # as this tool's companion article, which has no column picker and
  # colors its points the moment its one compute cell runs.
  preview_col <- if ("soil_moisture_pct" %in% numeric_cols) {
    "soil_moisture_pct"
  } else if (length(numeric_cols) > 0) {
    numeric_cols[1]
  } else {
    NA
  }

  preview_min <- NA
  preview_max <- NA
  pts_out <- pts
  if (!is.na(preview_col)) {
    preview_values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(sf::st_drop_geometry(pts)[[preview_col]])))
    finite_values <- preview_values[is.finite(preview_values)]
    if (length(finite_values) > 0) {
      preview_min <- min(finite_values)
      preview_max <- max(finite_values)
      pts_out$.previewValue <- preview_values
    }
  }

  summary_out <- list(
    count = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(pts)),
    crs = jsonlite::unbox(original_crs_label),
    columns = cols,
    numericColumns = numeric_cols,
    previewColumn = if (is.na(preview_col)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(preview_col),
    previewMin = if (is.na(preview_min)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(round(preview_min, 3)),
    previewMax = if (is.na(preview_max)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(round(preview_max, 3))
  )
  if (!is.null(crs_warning)) {
    summary_out$crsWarning <- jsonlite::unbox(crs_warning)
  }

  features_out <- jsonlite::fromJSON(sf_geojson(pts_out), simplifyVector = FALSE)
}

list(features = features_out, summary = summary_out)
```

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable
computation using `gstat::variogram()`, `fit.variogram()` and
`krige()` underneath. Want to see the same pipeline built up one step
at a time, and why this tool runs on R, not Python? Read
[Interpolating Soil Moisture with Kriging](/posts/kriging-soil-sampling.html).

```{.webgeods-r #kriging-interpolator-compute-r .tool-cell}
#| inject: [valueColumn, variogramModel, gridResolution]
#| package: sf, gstat, geojsonsf, jsonlite
library(sf)
library(gstat)
library(geojsonsf)

pts <- NULL
for (path in c("/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip")) {
  pts <- tryCatch(st_read(path, quiet = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(pts)) break
}
if (is.na(st_crs(pts))) {
  pts <- st_set_crs(pts, 4326)
} else if (is.na(st_crs(pts)$epsg) || st_crs(pts)$epsg != 4326) {
  pts <- st_transform(pts, 4326)
}

value_col <- valueColumn
values_raw <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(sf::st_drop_geometry(pts)[[value_col]])))
value_mask <- !is.na(values_raw) & is.finite(values_raw)
pts <- pts[value_mask, ]
values_raw <- values_raw[value_mask]

if (nrow(pts) < 5) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Need at least 5 points with a valid numeric value in \"", value_col,
    "\" to fit a variogram — found ", nrow(pts), "."
  ))
}

# Working/calculation CRS: a variogram fit on raw degrees would treat 1
# degree of longitude and 1 degree of latitude as the same real
# distance everywhere on Earth, which they aren't -- same UTM auto-pick
# (bounding-box center) as this project's other vector tools.
bbox <- st_bbox(pts)
center_lon <- as.numeric((bbox["xmin"] + bbox["xmax"]) / 2)
center_lat <- as.numeric((bbox["ymin"] + bbox["ymax"]) / 2)
utm_zone <- floor((center_lon + 180) / 6) + 1
calc_epsg <- if (center_lat >= 0) 32600 + utm_zone else 32700 + utm_zone
calc_crs_label <- paste0("EPSG:", calc_epsg)

pts_calc <- st_transform(pts, calc_epsg)
pts_calc$.krige_value <- values_raw

v_emp <- variogram(.krige_value ~ 1, pts_calc)

init_range <- max(v_emp$dist) / 3
init_psill <- var(pts_calc$.krige_value)
v_model <- tryCatch(
  fit.variogram(
    v_emp,
    vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)
  ),
  error = function(e) NULL
)

if (is.null(v_model) || isTRUE(attr(v_model, "singular")) || any(v_model$psill < 0)) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Could not fit a ", variogramModel, " variogram model to this data ",
    "(often too few points, or no real spatial structure to find). ",
    "Try a different model, or more sample points."
  ))
}

v_line <- variogramLine(v_model, maxdist = max(v_emp$dist), n = 100)

# Prediction grid over the sample points' own extent, padded 5% on
# each side so the surface doesn't stop exactly at the outermost
# points. gridResolution cells along the LONGER side, same "cap the
# cell count regardless of extent" formula as this project's other
# grid-building tools (Spatial Classifier, e.g.).
bbc <- st_bbox(pts_calc)
pad_x <- as.numeric(bbc["xmax"] - bbc["xmin"]) * 0.05
pad_y <- as.numeric(bbc["ymax"] - bbc["ymin"]) * 0.05
gxmin <- as.numeric(bbc["xmin"]) - pad_x
gxmax <- as.numeric(bbc["xmax"]) + pad_x
gymin <- as.numeric(bbc["ymin"]) - pad_y
gymax <- as.numeric(bbc["ymax"]) + pad_y

longer_side <- max(gxmax - gxmin, gymax - gymin, 1e-6)
cell_size <- longer_side / as.numeric(gridResolution)
nx <- max(2, ceiling((gxmax - gxmin) / cell_size))
ny <- max(2, ceiling((gymax - gymin) / cell_size))

xs <- seq(gxmin, gxmax, length.out = nx)
# Decreasing -- north (max) first: setRasterImage's own row-major
# convention puts row 0 at the TOP of the image, i.e. the northernmost
# row (see shared/map-raster.js), so the grid has to be built in that
# same order rather than relying on any later reordering.
ys <- seq(gymax, gymin, length.out = ny)
# expand.grid varies its FIRST argument fastest -- x cycles through a
# full row before y advances one step -- which is exactly row-major
# order with x as the column index and y (already north-to-south) as
# the row index. krige() below preserves this row order in its output.
grid_df <- expand.grid(x = xs, y = ys)
grid_sf <- st_as_sf(grid_df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = calc_epsg)

k <- krige(.krige_value ~ 1, pts_calc, grid_sf, model = v_model, debug.level = 0)
pred <- as.numeric(k$var1.pred)
var_pred <- as.numeric(k$var1.var)

grid_bbox_calc <- st_sfc(
  st_polygon(list(matrix(
    c(gxmin, gymin, gxmax, gymin, gxmax, gymax, gxmin, gymax, gxmin, gymin),
    ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE
  ))),
  crs = calc_epsg
)
bb_wgs84 <- st_bbox(st_transform(grid_bbox_calc, 4326))

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(pred, con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
pred_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

pts_wgs84 <- st_transform(pts_calc, 4326)
pts_wgs84$value <- pts_wgs84$.krige_value
pts_out <- pts_wgs84[, "value"]

result_out <- list(
  summary = list(
    count = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(pts_calc)),
    calculationCrs = jsonlite::unbox(calc_crs_label),
    valueColumn = jsonlite::unbox(value_col),
    variogramModel = jsonlite::unbox(variogramModel),
    nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(v_model$psill[1], 4)),
    partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(v_model$psill[2], 4)),
    range = jsonlite::unbox(round(v_model$range[2], 1)),
    gridResolution = jsonlite::unbox(as.numeric(gridResolution)),
    gridCellCount = jsonlite::unbox(length(pred)),
    meanPrediction = jsonlite::unbox(round(mean(pred, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
    meanVariance = jsonlite::unbox(round(mean(var_pred, na.rm = TRUE), 4))
  ),
  variogram = list(
    empirical = list(dist = round(v_emp$dist, 2), gamma = round(v_emp$gamma, 5), npairs = v_emp$np),
    fitted = list(dist = round(v_line$dist, 2), gamma = round(v_line$gamma, 5))
  ),
  raster = list(
    width = jsonlite::unbox(nx),
    height = jsonlite::unbox(ny),
    data = jsonlite::unbox(pred_b64),
    wgs84Bounds = round(c(bb_wgs84["xmin"], bb_wgs84["ymin"], bb_wgs84["xmax"], bb_wgs84["ymax"]), 6),
    min = jsonlite::unbox(round(min(pred, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
    max = jsonlite::unbox(round(max(pred, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
  )
)

out <- jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result_out, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
# Attached AFTER the round-trip above, not inside it: sf_geojson()
# already returns finished JSON, and a second toJSON() pass would turn
# every scalar inside it back into a one-element array (same reasoning
# as spatial-classification.qmd's own compute cell).
out$samplePoints <- jsonlite::fromJSON(sf_geojson(pts_out), simplifyVector = FALSE)
out
```

```{.webgeods-r #kriging-interpolator-export-r .tool-cell}
#| inject: [valueColumn, variogramModel, gridResolution]
#| package: sf, gstat, terra, jsonlite
# Recomputes the same kriging pipeline (cheap relative to re-reading
# the source file) and writes it as an actual GeoTIFF via
# terra::writeRaster() -- in the CALCULATION crs (the projection the
# computation actually ran in), not the original file's CRS, since
# re-reprojecting the result back just for convenience would add a
# step with no real benefit -- the download button below labels this
# explicitly. Same reasoning and structure as
# viewshed-calculator.qmd's own export cell.
library(sf)
library(gstat)
library(terra)

pts <- NULL
for (path in c("/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip")) {
  pts <- tryCatch(st_read(path, quiet = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(pts)) break
}
if (is.na(st_crs(pts))) {
  pts <- st_set_crs(pts, 4326)
} else if (is.na(st_crs(pts)$epsg) || st_crs(pts)$epsg != 4326) {
  pts <- st_transform(pts, 4326)
}

value_col <- valueColumn
values_raw <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(sf::st_drop_geometry(pts)[[value_col]])))
value_mask <- !is.na(values_raw) & is.finite(values_raw)
pts <- pts[value_mask, ]
values_raw <- values_raw[value_mask]

bbox <- st_bbox(pts)
center_lon <- as.numeric((bbox["xmin"] + bbox["xmax"]) / 2)
center_lat <- as.numeric((bbox["ymin"] + bbox["ymax"]) / 2)
utm_zone <- floor((center_lon + 180) / 6) + 1
calc_epsg <- if (center_lat >= 0) 32600 + utm_zone else 32700 + utm_zone

pts_calc <- st_transform(pts, calc_epsg)
pts_calc$.krige_value <- values_raw

v_emp <- variogram(.krige_value ~ 1, pts_calc)
init_range <- max(v_emp$dist) / 3
init_psill <- var(pts_calc$.krige_value)
v_model <- fit.variogram(
  v_emp,
  vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)
)

bbc <- st_bbox(pts_calc)
pad_x <- as.numeric(bbc["xmax"] - bbc["xmin"]) * 0.05
pad_y <- as.numeric(bbc["ymax"] - bbc["ymin"]) * 0.05
gxmin <- as.numeric(bbc["xmin"]) - pad_x
gxmax <- as.numeric(bbc["xmax"]) + pad_x
gymin <- as.numeric(bbc["ymin"]) - pad_y
gymax <- as.numeric(bbc["ymax"]) + pad_y

longer_side <- max(gxmax - gxmin, gymax - gymin, 1e-6)
cell_size <- longer_side / as.numeric(gridResolution)
nx <- max(2, ceiling((gxmax - gxmin) / cell_size))
ny <- max(2, ceiling((gymax - gymin) / cell_size))

xs <- seq(gxmin, gxmax, length.out = nx)
ys <- seq(gymax, gymin, length.out = ny)
grid_df <- expand.grid(x = xs, y = ys)
grid_sf <- st_as_sf(grid_df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = calc_epsg)

k <- krige(.krige_value ~ 1, pts_calc, grid_sf, model = v_model, debug.level = 0)
pred <- as.numeric(k$var1.pred)

# expand.grid above cycles x fastest, y north-to-south -- exactly
# terra's own row-major convention for a matrix passed to rast()
# (row 1 = the top/north row), so no reordering is needed here beyond
# reshaping the flat vector.
pred_matrix <- matrix(pred, nrow = ny, ncol = nx, byrow = TRUE)
r <- rast(pred_matrix, extent = ext(gxmin, gxmax, gymin, gymax), crs = paste0("EPSG:", calc_epsg))
names(r) <- value_col

out_path <- "/tmp/kriging.tif"
writeRaster(r, out_path, overwrite = TRUE, filetype = "GTiff")
raw_bytes <- readBin(out_path, what = "raw", n = file.info(out_path)$size)
jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)
```

*First run loads the R engine — expect 1-3 minutes (R's WebAssembly
build is noticeably slower to start than this site's Python tools).
Instant after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*

First tool in the GeoStatistics family. The green dots are your own
sample points (brown = low, teal = high, on the same scale as the
surface underneath); the colored surface is the prediction everywhere
else. Want the code, or why this runs on R, not Python? Read the
<a href="/posts/kriging-soil-sampling.html">full article</a>. Got a
raster with gaps instead of scattered points — a cloud-covered
satellite band, say? The

same variogram fitting, but fills an existing grid's own holes instead
of predicting one from scratch. Recorded a category instead of a
number (soil type, habitat)? The
<a href="/tools/spatial-classifier.html">Spatial Classifier</a> maps
that across the area instead.
